title: NH3-SCR DeNOx reference family
objective: Optional literature-backed reference family for sanity-checking catalyst economics for selective catalytic reduction of NOx with ammonia, covering stationary oxide monoliths and mobile zeolite washcoats. COMET itself remains reaction-agnostic and this family is a screening aid, not a process design.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Balance economics, source confidence, route confidence, and performance.

cost-first.label: Cost-first
cost-first.description: Bias ranking toward selling cost while keeping route and evidence guardrails.

evidence-first.label: Evidence-first
evidence-first.description: Reward transparent, higher-confidence pricing and more reproducible routes.

citations.label: Appl. Catal. B 1998
citations.note: Busca's classic review of the chemistry of oxide-based NH3-SCR catalysis.

citations.label: Appl. Catal. A 2001
citations.note: Forzatti's status review of commercial de-NOx SCR including V2O5-WO3/TiO2 honeycomb practice.

citations.label: Catalysts 2015
citations.note: Vanadium-loading optimization across 1.7-3.5 wt% V2O5 with the optimum at 2.0-2.6 wt%.

citations.label: Catalysts 2019
citations.note: Commercial tail-end SCR monolith operated around 200 C for 18,000 h. XRF of the virgin material gives 3.51 wt% V2O5 and 6.36 wt% WO3 (oxide basis); this is not the screened 2.5/7/90.5 formulation.

citations.label: J. Catal. 2010
citations.note: Kwak et al.: the discovery-scale demonstration of Cu-SSZ-13 activity and selectivity for NOx SCR.

citations.label: Top. Catal. 2013
citations.note: Cu-chabazite as the commercially deployed diesel DeNOx catalyst.

citations.label: Science 2017
citations.note: Dynamic multinuclear Cu sites govern low-temperature SCR in Cu-CHA.

citations.label: Chem. Soc. Rev. 2018
citations.note: Cu-CHA as an industrially applied model system; Si/Al and Cu/Al ratios control performance.

citations.label: J. Catal. 1999
citations.note: Long and Yang's Fe-ZSM-5 NH3-SCR benchmark study.

citations.label: Catal. Rev. 2008
citations.note: State-of-the-art review of metal-exchanged zeolite SCR; isolated Fe sites the most active, TOF falls at higher Fe content.

citations.label: Catalysts 2020
citations.note: Review of Fe/SSZ-13, Fe/SAPO-34, Fe/SSZ-39 and Fe/LTA. Its small-pore stability comparison is context, not direct performance evidence for medium-pore Fe-ZSM-5.

citations.label: Chem. Soc. Rev. 2015
citations.note: Beale's review of small-pore zeolites for NOx control.

citations.label: Appl. Sci. 2021
citations.note: Experimental stereolithography-printed alumina lattices washcoated with V2O5-WO3-TiO2 and compared with cordierite honeycombs; evidence for a specific substrate study, not a commercial production recipe.

route_templates.name: V-W impregnation on titania with honeycomb forming
route_templates.manufacturing_mode: Full-body extruded or washcoated honeycomb monolith
preprocess: Tungsten and vanadium precursor solution make-up
synthesis: Sequential W then V impregnation onto the titania
quality_gates: V2O5 loading confirmation (2.0-2.6 wt% optimum band)
NO conversion spot test at 300 C
route_templates.route_note: Impregnation and forming chain grounded in the cited studies; full-body extrusion of V-W-Ti honeycombs is standard commercial practice per Forzatti's review (full-text claim).

route_templates.name: Cu ion exchange into SSZ-13 with washcoating
preprocess: SSZ-13 (CHA) zeolite synthesis with organic template
synthesis: Liquid ion exchange of Cu into the zeolite
postprocess: Washcoat slurry preparation and coating onto cordierite
route_templates.route_note: Zeolite synthesis dominates the cost; the SSZ-13 template chemistry is priced inside the material term, and washcoating follows commercial honeycomb practice.

route_templates.name: Fe ion exchange into ZSM-5 with washcoating
synthesis: Liquid ion exchange of Fe into the zeolite
route_templates.route_note: Simpler than the Cu-CHA chain because commodity ZSM-5 replaces the template-heavy small-pore synthesis.

candidates.title: V2O5-WO3/TiO2 monolith (stationary standard)
candidates.summary: V-W/TiO2 stationary SCR cost proxy. A separate commercial monolith study documents 18,000 h of tail-end service around 200 C with a different measured oxide composition.
decision_notes: The retained 2.5 wt% V2O5, 7 wt% WO3 and 90.5 wt% TiO2 are screening inputs. The service study instead reports 3.51 wt% V2O5 and 6.36 wt% WO3, plus reinforcing fibers and other constituents.

The 260-420 C screening window is not the approximately 200 C service temperature in the 18,000 h case. Catalyst-grade anatase, forming aids, monolith geometry and price parity with TiO2 pigment remain assumptions.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

pricing.note: Annual average WO3 concentrate price 2024, $25/kg = $11.34/lb (USGS MCS 2025).
2025e landed duty-paid unit value of U.S. TiO2 pigment imports, $3,200/t (USGS MCS Feb 2026); anatase SCR grade carried at pigment parity.

candidates.title: Cu-SSZ-13 (diesel aftertreatment standard)
candidates.summary: Copper-exchanged small-pore chabazite: the commercially deployed diesel SCR catalyst with a wide 200-500 C window, high N2 selectivity, and the hydrothermal durability that put it in production trucks.
decision_notes: The primary Cu-SSZ-13 study establishes the architecture and activity/selectivity relative to Cu-beta and Cu-ZSM-5, but the exact 2.5 wt% Cu recipe was not verified from accessible primary experimental text.

Cu loading, Si/Al ratio, hydrothermal-aging conditions, washcoat/substrate mass and the 200-500 C screening window must be specified for a quantitative comparison. The SSZ-13 material price remains an engineering proxy.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

pricing.note: Cu market basis with an assumed precursor markup; the retained 2.5 wt% loading is a screening input, not a newly verified experimental composition.

Template-intensive small-pore zeolite proxy. Public bracket: UN Comtrade synthetic-silicate imports $4.07/kg and commodity-zeolite marketplace offers $4.50-5.50/kg sit below it because the SSZ-13 trimethyladamantammonium template dominates cost; no public SSZ-13 quote was verified.

candidates.title: Fe-ZSM-5 high-temperature variant
candidates.summary: Fe-ZSM-5 screening archetype with primary evidence for high-temperature NH3-SCR; comparisons with Cu catalysts require matched zeolite topology, loading and reaction conditions.
decision_notes: The Long-Yang primary abstract reports nearly complete NO conversion at 400-500 C and strong exchange-level and Si/Al effects; it does not establish the retained 2 wt% Fe recipe or 300-550 C window.

The Fe small-pore-zeolite review concerns other framework types and does not prove superior stability of this ZSM-5 candidate. Generic ion exchange, commodity support pricing and isolated-Fe speciation remain assumptions.
Performance, readiness and route scores are authored screening assessments, not measured conversion, selectivity or lifetime; price-evidence scores assess pricing provenance separately.

pricing.note: Contained-Fe cost from bulk synthetic black iron oxide (ICIS 2006, $0.94/lb, CatCost library), ChemPPI-escalated. The scrap-iron market feed understates precursor chemistry ~40x, so Fe components price on a precursor basis.

pricing.evidence_label: UN Comtrade synthetic-silicate import unit value
pricing.note: 2024 U.S. imports of HS 2842.10 (the synthetic-zeolite trade code): $143.53M / 35.27M kg = $4.07/kg CIF. Code is broader than zeolites alone; bulk marketplace ZSM-5 offers at $4.50-5.50/kg corroborate the level.
